prompt: Add optimistic updates to a TanStack Query mutation for liking a post.
assertions: The mutation implements the three-step onMutate/onError/onSettled shape, in that order, matching the cancel-snapshot-write → rollback → invalidate discipline.
onMutate cancels in-flight queries for the affected key (e.g. via queryClient.cancelQueries) before snapshotting and applying the optimistic value.
onError rolls back to the snapshot taken in onMutate.
onSettled invalidates the query regardless of outcome.

prompt: Build an accessible form with an inline validation error on the email field.
assertions: The error message is associated with its input via aria-describedby, and aria-invalid is set while the error is showing.
The submit button stays enabled while the form is invalid; validation runs on submit rather than disabling the button preemptively.
Focus moves to the first invalid field (or a focusable error summary) after a failed submission.

prompt: Style the headline and body text on this SwiftUI screen.
assertions: Text uses semantic text styles (.font(.headline), .font(.body), etc.) rather than .font(.system(size:)) with a hardcoded point value.
The layout is described as reflowing at large accessibility Dynamic Type sizes rather than truncating or clipping.

prompt: Fix layout shift caused by an image and a web font loading late on this landing page.
assertions: The image fix reserves layout space up front via explicit width/height or aspect-ratio rather than letting the image load in without dimensions.
The font-loading fix names an explicit font-display value (or an equivalent matched-fallback strategy) chosen for its CLS risk, not left at the browser default.

prompt: Wire the handoff.yaml tokens into this component, including a dark-mode variant.
assertions: Tokens are consumed from the generated token layer; the generated output file itself is not hand-edited.
Dark mode is implemented via a single, stated token strategy rather than ad hoc per-component overrides.
The dark-mode variant is called out as needing its own verification rather than assumed correct because light mode passed.

prompt: Rebuild the client's existing marketing site on Next.js; some hero photos failed to download and the logo is a PNG.
assertions: The captured logo is rendered as the image file, not replaced by a text wordmark.

Missing hero photos are recovered (lazy-load data attributes, srcset, computed backgrounds, owner originals) or shown as an explicit labeled placeholder reported as a gap — never swapped for unrelated stock imagery.
Acceptance is a pixel-diff parity check against reference screenshots of the source at fixed viewports, with the threshold stated before comparison, not an eyeballed review.
An interactive source widget (e.g. the hero slider) is built as working behavior, not a static image.

prompt: Wire a streaming agent-run view in our Next.js app over the product's run event stream, with an approval card for actions.
assertions: The UI renders the product's versioned run events, not a vendor UI-library message format as the contract.
Reconnect subscribes after the last committed event ID and applies replays idempotently; an expired cursor is replaced by a server snapshot.
Partial streamed text is shown as provisional and replaced, not appended, when a retried step commits.
Closing the tab or unmounting closes the stream only; cancel and approve are authenticated API calls with an idempotency key.
The approval card shows the exact operation, target, normalized parameters, and expiry from the approval event.
